source_text: Malum autem quod agit, a possibili agit.
pass_a_gloss: But the evil which he does, he does from the possible.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: The evil he does, however, he does from possibility.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
